questions.question_text: Estimate $4.2 \times 7$ by rounding the decimal factor to a whole number.

options.why: Rounded 4.2 up to 5 instead of to the nearer whole number 4.
Added 7 to 4.2 instead of multiplying the rounded factor by 7.
Multiplied 42 by 7 without accounting for the decimal place or estimating first.

questions.question_text:
The product $8.9 \times 6$ is closest to $54$.
Which statement best locates the exact product?

options.why: Treated 8.9 as greater than 9, although it is slightly less than 9.
Rounds $8.9$ down to $8$, calculates $8 \times 6=48$, then treats the rough product as exact.
Rounded 8.9 to 9 correctly but then treated the estimate as the exact product.

questions.solution_text:
$8.9<9$
$8.9 \times 6<9 \times 6$
$8.9 \times 6<54$
The product is slightly less than $54$.

questions.question_text:
A calculator is used for $3.07 \times 8$.
Which display has a reasonable magnitude?

options.why: Placed the decimal point one place too far left, giving a value far below the estimate of about 24.
Placed the decimal point one place too far right, giving a value about ten times the estimate.
Ignored all decimal places, giving a value about one hundred times the estimate.

questions.question_text: Nine samples each have a mass of $0.62$ g. Which is the closest estimate of their total mass?

options.why: Rounded 0.62 to 1 but did not multiply the rounded value by nine samples.
Treated 0.62 as about 6, making the estimate ten times too large.
Ignored both decimal places and treated 0.62 as about 60.

questions.solution_text:
$0.62\text{ g} \approx 0.6\text{ g}$
$0.6 \times 9$
$=5.4$
The closest estimate is $6$ g.

questions.question_text: Without finding the exact value, between which consecutive multiples of $5$ does $12.4 \times 5$ lie?

options.why: Bounded 12.4 between 11 and 12 instead of between 12 and 13.
Bounded 12.4 between 13 and 14, shifting both whole-number bounds up by one.
Used multiples of 10 rather than multiplying the bounding whole numbers by 5.

questions.question_text:
The calculator digits for $18.06 \times 7$ are $12642$, but the decimal point is missing.
Use an estimate to choose the correct display.

options.why: Placed the point one place too far left, giving a result about ten times smaller than the estimate.
Placed the point one place too far right, giving a result about ten times larger than the estimate.
Placed the point two places too far left, giving a result about one hundred times too small.
